entries.reason: IMPLEMENTED in packages/a/apple-backports/PDFKit/PDFAnnotationColours11.m and MEASURED over 48 named fixtures, and NOT COMPARABLE on this machine.  The key is /MK's /BG - /BC is the BORDER colour of Table 8.40 and is what -border reads, and bg-bc-beside carries both and answers the /BG, as PDFAnnotationUtilities.h:280 says of backgroundColor ('Used by annotations type(s): /Widget').  One component answers kCGColorSpaceDeviceGray, three kCGColorSpaceDeviceRGB and four kCGColorSpaceDeviceCMYK, with the ARRAY'S OWN components and an alpha of 1: [1 0 0] answers 1, 0, 0, 1 in DeviceRGB, and an earlier version of this row that printed 0.986, 0, 0.027 had converted that to sRGB in its own probe, which is a reading of the probe.  [0 0 0 0] answers a DeviceCMYK colour of four zeros, NOT white.  (a string) is nil, /FT /Btn answers DeviceRGB blue, and a /Ch with no /Opt is NOT SURFACED AT ALL by -[PDFPage annotations]' choice-widget skip - which is what the earlier claim of a /Ch answering a green its array does not contain actually was: the next annotation's /BG, read one index out of step.  WHY NOT COMPARABLE: the only macOS binary with a UIColor is the Catalyst one, it links no PDFKit (otool -L) and still loads /System/iOSSupport/.../PDFKit.framework at run time - 14 'implemented in both' lines - and the platform declares this same selector on its own PDFAnnotationUtilities category, which REPLACES the port's because a category in a later image wins.  That it is the category and not the port is measured: a -777 sentinel in PDFAppearanceCharacteristics' own -init answered appearance.fresh.controlType=-777 in the same binary, so the class's own members there do run. The three cannot move into the class's own @implementation either - PDFPage's and PDFAnnotation's ivars are declared in PDFAnnotation11.m and a class has one @implementation, so a second object can only add a CATEGORY, and it needs UIKit, which the macOS port side has not got.  The row is inert for that and not for want of a reading

entries.reason: the key and the whole rule are ESTABLISHED, and the member is NOT CARRIED at all for a reason of its own.  It reads the /DA's FILL operand, and only a fill one, which is the format's rule and not a gap: text is painted with the fill colour, so g and rg are read and G, RG and K - which set the stroke - are not.  MEASURED, keyed by /NM: (0 g) answers kCGColorSpaceGenericGray 0, 1 and (1 g) the same space at 1, 1; (1 0 0 rg) answers kCGColorSpaceGenericRGB 1, 0, 0, 1; and BOTH CMYK values, whose conversions are red and cyan, answer the gray default, so k is not read either.  The operand's POSITION is settled and it is the FIRST that decides: `0.5 g 1 0 0 rg' answers the gray and `1 0 0 rg 0.5 g' answers the RGB; and a colour operator with the wrong operand count is not refused but reads the numbers in front of it, so `0.5 0.25 g' answers 0.25.  An annotation with NO /DA and a /DA with no readable fill are TWO DIFFERENT DEFAULTS - kCGColorSpaceGenericGrayGamma2_2 against kCGColorSpaceGenericGray.  WHY IT IS NOT CARRIED: those three colour-space NAMES are API_AVAILABLE(ios(9.0)) in this SDK while the row's minimum is 6.0, and CGColorSpaceCreateWithName - the mechanism, and itself iOS 2.0 - would be handed names a 6.1.3 CoreGraphics does not have, so a port calling them would build a dylib that cannot load on its own minimum release.  A measurement of which release first EXPORTS each name, from the held caches' export tries through tools/symbol-first-release.lua, was queued and did not come back, so no claim is made here about what 6.1.3 exports - only about what this SDK annotates.  The member's host values are still printed by the harness, because a measurement is worth keeping where the port has no answer to set against it
